To maintain contact between the sample and the pushrod of the dilatometer, a constant vertical force of 100 mN is exerted on the sample throughout the measurement. During the experiment, the change in the sample's length is tracked over time as a potential is applied to control hydrogen concentration. The same sample was measured three times under identical experimental conditions, using the same instrument setup and measurement protocol. Temperature is recorded simultaneously using a thermocouple, and the first derivative of the length change with respect to time (dL/dt) is used as a measure of the flux.

candidates.permitted_context_evidence: This dataset contains the time-dependent length change of nanoporous Palladium during hydrogen charging and discharging. The electrochemical protocol consists of a chronoamperometric potential step held at 40 mV vs. RHE for 4200 s, followed by a second step to 120 mV vs. RHE for 1200 s. The time step for the length change measurement is set to 0.1 s. A vertical dilatometer (Linseis L75V) is combined with an electrochemical setup to monitor the in situ length variation of the nanoporous Pd sample during hydrogen charging and discharging. The working electrode, reference electrode, and counter electrode are the sample connected to a gold wire, RHE, and carbon cloth, respectively. The electrolyte is 1.0 M H2SO4. To maintain contact between the sample and the pushrod of the dilatometer, a constant vertical force of 100 mN is exerted on the sample throughout the measurement. During the experiment, the change in the sample's length is tracked over time as a potential is applied to control hydrogen concentration. The same sample was measured three times under identical experimental conditions, using the same instrument setup and measurement protocol. Temperature is recorded simultaneously using a thermocouple, and the first derivative of the length change with respect to time (dL/dt) is used as a measure of the flux.
